title_jp: {受付|うけつけ}の{仕事|しごと}
context: Now you're on the other side of the desk, welcoming guests at the hostel where you volunteer.

phrases.jp: ご{予約|よやく}のお{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
phrases.en: May I have the name on the reservation?

phrases.jp: {少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。
phrases.note: The most-used phrase in Japanese service. Say it whenever you need time.

phrases.jp: こちらにご{記入|きにゅう}ください。
{朝食|ちょうしょく}は7{時|じ}から9{時|じ}までです。
{今日|きょう}、{満室|まんしつ}だって。
phrases.note: ～だって = "I heard that…", to a coworker.

dialogue_setting: Behind the reception desk, a guest walks in without a booking.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.jp: すみません、{今夜|こんや}{空|あ}いてる{部屋|へや}ありますか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, do you have a room free tonight?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。…はい、ドミトリーでしたら{空|あ}いています。
dialogue.en: One moment, please… Yes, we have a dorm bed free.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、お{願|ねが}いします。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: ありがとうございます。こちらにご{記入|きにゅう}ください。
dialogue.en: Thank you. Please fill this in.

kanji.where: On hotel signs and booking sites. The opposite is {空室|くうしつ}あり (rooms available).

tip.title: Learn service phrases as blocks
tip.body: At work you'll use fixed polite phrases: かしこまりました (certainly), {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません (I'm very sorry), ございます. Learn them as blocks; nobody expects you to build keigo from scratch. A smile and a clear voice matter more than perfect grammar.

challenge.prompt: A guest asks something you don't understand. Say: "I'm very sorry, one moment please. I'll call the manager."
challenge.hint: manager = {責任者|せきにんしゃ}, go and call = {呼|よ}んできます
challenge.model_answer: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません、{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。{責任者|せきにんしゃ}を{呼|よ}んできます。
